# API contract

> **Closed list.** Every callable name is below; anything else does not exist on the robot. Generated from `contract/semantics.json`; full reference with the same content: [../docs/reference/api.md](../docs/reference/api.md). Limits: [constraints.md](constraints.md).

Globals: `Engine` `Timer` `print` `Input` `Sprite` `Text` `Shape` `Anim` `Speaker` `Servo` `Led` `Voice` `Ranking`.

## Conventions

- **Failure modes.** Each call fails in one of these ways, shown in the *Bad argument* and *Failure* columns: **raise** (throws a Lua error; uncaught it aborts the hook, see [Hooks](../docs/reference/api.md#hooks) for what that does), **false** (returns `false`), **nil, reason** (returns `nil` and a string; test the first value), **no-op** (does nothing).
- **Families.** Display and input (`Sprite`, `Text`, `Shape`, `Anim`, `Input`) raise on a wrong argument type. Robot peripherals (`Speaker`, `Servo`, `Led`) never raise: a bad argument returns `false`. `Voice.set_keywords` raises on a non-table list. Status calls (`Timer`, `Ranking`, `Engine`, `print`) validate little.
- **Integers.** Arguments documented as integers (`x`, `y`, `w`, `h`, `z`, frame index, Shape coordinates, scale, rotation) raise `number has no integer representation` on a fractional number. `2.0` is accepted. Round with `math.floor(x + 0.5)`.
- **Integers are 32-bit on the robot** (`LUA_USE_C89`): `math.maxinteger` is 2^31−1 and integer overflow wraps. Floats are doubles.
- **Handles.** `Sprite`, `Text`, `Shape` and `Anim` are userdata; call methods with a colon (`spr:set_pos(x, y)`). `:destroy()` is idempotent; after it every method is a no-op (getters return zeros, boolean methods `false`). Text and Shape no-ops log a warning; Sprite and Anim no-ops are silent.
- **Keep a reference to every handle.** Handles have `__gc`: a Sprite, Text, Shape or Anim that no Lua variable references is destroyed at the next garbage collection and disappears from the screen. A dropped Text or Shape keeps its pool slot until then. Handles also support `<close>`. Everything is freed when the game ends.
- **Paths** are relative to the pack folder. The engine prefixes `/sd/games/<game_id>/`; the whole path must stay under 200 bytes, so a relative path may use at most 188 bytes minus the length of the game id. An absolute path, a backslash, a control character, or an empty, `.` or `..` segment (`a//b`, trailing `/`) raises `unsafe ... path`.
- **Colours.** `Text` and `Shape` take `0xRRGGBB`. `Sprite.solid` takes 16-bit RGB565. Mixing them gives wrong colours, not an error.
- **Reading an unknown field** of an engine global or handle gives `nil` (feature detection works); calling it raises. `pika` is an empty global table.

## Hooks

Define hooks as globals in the entry script; all are optional. Each call runs under the hook watchdog (1500 ms); a call that runs longer raises `watchdog: Lua pcall exceeded ...`. The watchdog is checked every 4000 Lua instructions, so one long native call (a big image load) is only caught when it returns. A separate stall detector ends a game whose frame loop makes no progress for 5 s.

| Hook | Bound | If it raises |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `game_start(params)` | looked up at call | Load fails (`game.error phase=load`); `game_end` is not called. |
| `on_tick(dt_ms)` | **once**, right after the top level runs | Game ends. |
| `on_input(action, phase, hold_ms)` | **once**, right after the top level runs | Game ends. |
| `on_input_lost(count)` | looked up at call | Game ends. |
| `on_sound_end(alias, reason)` | looked up at call | Game ends. |
| `on_sound_lost(count)` | looked up at call | Game ends. |
| `on_voice_event(e)` | looked up at call | Logged; the game continues (the session still reports `end=err`). |
| `on_home()` | looked up at call | Game ends (clean exit). `nil`, `false` or a missing hook also end it. |
| `game_end()` | looked up at call | Ignored. |
| `on_pack_cmd(cmd)` | looked up at call | Ignored. |

- **Define `on_tick` and `on_input` at the top level of the entry script.** They are bound once, before `game_start` runs; assigning them later (`on_tick = play_tick` inside `game_start` or a scene change) is silently ignored. Switch behaviour with a state variable inside one `on_tick`. Other hooks are looked up at every call.
- **Frame order.** Each frame: `on_sound_end`/`on_sound_lost` → `on_input`/`on_input_lost` → `on_tick` → queued servo, LED and sound-stop commands are sent → the active `Anim` advances at most one frame → all display changes are published as one screen update. `on_voice_event` and `on_home` run between frames.
- **The display lock is held for the whole tick.** Everything from the sound drain to the screen publish runs under the LVGL lock, so an SD read (`set_frame`), a PNG decode or a long Lua loop in a hook also freezes screen refresh for that time.
- **HOME held for 1500 ms or longer force-exits** the game whatever `on_home` returns (`end=home`). Only short presses reach `on_home`.
- `dt_ms` is always 33 (1000 / 30), not the measured frame time.
- The frame period is 30 ms: the RTOS tick is 10 ms, so the 33 ms target rounds down to whole ticks. That caps the loop at about 33 frames per second. A game that adds `dt_ms` every frame therefore runs about 10% fast when frames are on time and slow when they are late. **Use `Timer.millis()` for anything time-based.**

`params`: `is_a2a` (boolean): `true` when the game was started inside a talk-flow (A2A) session.; `language` (string): ISO 639-1 code of the robot's UI language, e.g. `"en"`.; `other fields` (any): Start parameters from the server, decoded from JSON: at most 127 bytes and 32 nodes. Longer, malformed or non-object parameters give an empty table plus the two fields above.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |

| `Engine.exit([reason])` | nothing | raise if `reason` is not a string or number | Schedules a normal stop; the current hook runs to its end, so `return` right after the call. |

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |

## Input

Buttons are addressed by the action names declared in `manifest.json` (`input.actions`). Without that block the engine defines `confirm` (enter), `left` and `right`. The robot has three game buttons: `button:left`, `button:enter`, `button:right`. HOME is not an action; it calls `on_home()`.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input.is_down(action)` | boolean | raise if `action` is missing or not a string; `false` for an unknown action | `true` while any button bound to the action is held. |
| `Input.just_pressed(action)` | boolean | raise; `false` | `true` in the frame the button went down. |
| `Input.just_released(action)` | boolean | raise; `false` | `true` in the frame the button went up. |
| `Input.hold_ms(action)` | integer | raise; `0` | Hold time carried by the last `REPEAT`/`RELEASE` event: `0` until the first `REPEAT` (400 ms after the press, then every 80 ms), kept at the release value after `RELEASE`, at most 65535. |
| `Input.actions()` | table | — | Array of action names in manifest order. |
| `Input.stats()` | table | — | `{events_total, events_delta, dropped_total, seq_gaps}`. |

Constants: `Input.PRESS`, `Input.RELEASE`, `Input.REPEAT`. Compare with the constants, never with numbers.

## Sprite

Images on the 480 × 320 screen. There is no sprite count limit; free PSRAM is the limit. PSRAM per sprite: `w*h*3` bytes for a PNG that can carry transparency (RGBA, grey+alpha, or any PNG with a `tRNS` chunk; RGB565 plus an 8-bit alpha plane), `w*h*2` for a PNG without alpha (RGB, grey or palette without `tRNS`), a raw `.rgb565` file or a solid. The engine decides from the PNG header, so an RGBA PNG whose alpha is always 255 still costs `w*h*3`: export opaque images as RGB PNG or `.rgb565`. While a PNG decodes, the whole file is also held in PSRAM.

A new sprite is placed at (0, 0) on top of everything created before it, but **stays hidden until its first `:set_pos` or `:set_visible`**. A sprite you never position is never drawn.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Sprite.image(path)` | sprite | raise on a non-string or unsafe path; nil, msg: e.g. `image load failed: assets/a.png (ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND)` or `(ESP_ERR_NO_MEM)` | Decodes a PNG, keeping its alpha. |
| `Sprite.new(path, w, h)` | sprite | raise on a non-string or unsafe path, or non-integer `w`/`h`; nil, msg | Loads raw RGB565 pixels (2 bytes per pixel, little-endian, row-major, no header); the file must hold at least `w*h*2` bytes. |
| `Sprite.solid(w, h, rgb565)` | sprite | raise when `w` is not 1..480 or `h` not 1..320; nil, `"oom"` or `"sprite create failed"` | Filled rectangle, no file. |
| `spr:set_pos(x, y)` | nothing | raise on non-integer | Top-left corner in screen pixels; off-screen is allowed. |
| `spr:get_pos()` | x, y | raise if `spr` is not a sprite |  |
| `spr:get_size()` | w, h | raise | Source size; `set_scale` does not change it. |
| `spr:set_visible(b)` | nothing | raise | Truthiness of `b`. |
| `spr:set_opacity(a)` | nothing | raise on non-number | 0..255, rounded and clamped. |
| `spr:set_z(i)` | nothing | raise on non-integer | Moves the object to child index `i` of the screen. |
| `spr:to_front()` | nothing | raise | Same as the highest index. |
| `spr:to_back()` | nothing | raise | Same as index 0. |
| `spr:set_flip(h, v)` | boolean | raise; `false` | Sets the absolute flip state (not a toggle) by rewriting every pixel (O(w·h)), and only when the state differs from the recorded one. |
| `spr:set_frame(path, i)` | boolean | raise on unsafe path or non-integer `i`; `false` when the file is missing or `i` is past the end | Overwrites the pixels with frame `i` (0-based) of a **raw strip file**: frames stored back to back in the sprite's own pixel format, `w*h*2` bytes per frame for `Sprite.new`, `Sprite.solid` and an opaque PNG sprite, `w*h*3` for a PNG sprite with alpha. |
| `spr:set_scale(n)` | boolean | raise on non-integer; `false` when the sprite is too large to transform | `256` = 1×, `512` = 2×, `128` = ½×. |
| `spr:set_rotation(deg10)` | boolean | raise on non-integer; `false` when the sprite is too large to transform | Tenths of a degree (`900` = 90°), wraps modulo 3600. |
| `spr:set_pivot(x, y)` | boolean | raise on non-integer | Origin of scale and rotation in sprite-local pixels; default is the centre. |
| `spr:hit_test(x, y)` | boolean | raise | Point inside `[x, x+w) × [y, y+h)`. |
| `spr:intersects(other)` | boolean | raise if `other` is not a sprite | Axis-aligned rectangles overlap. |
| `spr:destroy()` | nothing | — | Frees the pixels now. |

## Text

Retained text labels. At most 8 exist at a time (`text_slots`). Text does not wrap and there is no width query: break lines in your data with `\n` and check the longest string in the simulator.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Text.new(str, x, y)` | text | raise on non-string `str` or non-integer `x`/`y`; nil, `"pool_full"` (8 labels live, or out of memory) or `"text_create_failed"` | Shown immediately, top-left at (x, y), white, default font. |
| `t:set(str)` | nothing | raise on non-string; no-op on a destroyed label | Changes the text. |
| `t:move(x, y)` | nothing | raise on non-integer; no-op | Absolute top-left position. |
| `t:align(where[, dx, dy])` | nothing | raise on non-string `where`; nil, `"unknown Text align: ..."` or `"stale_text"` | Aligns to the screen. |
| `t:set_font(path[, size])` | nothing | raise on non-string `path`; nil, msg: unsafe path, bad file, stale label, or font cache full | TrueType font from the pack, file at most 512 KiB. |
| `t:set_color(rgb)` | nothing | raise on non-integer; no-op | `0xRRGGBB`. |
| `t:show(b)` | nothing | raise; no-op | Show or hide. |
| `t:destroy()` | nothing | — | Frees the slot for a new `Text.new`. |

A face is a (path, size) pair. The engine caches at most 4 faces; labels using the same pair share one. A face used by a live label cannot be evicted, so a fifth distinct pair fails until a label using another face is destroyed or switched. Ship every font the pack uses; the default font does not cover every script.

Text has no `set_z`. Its stacking is its creation order, changed only when other objects call `:set_z`, `:to_front` or `:to_back`. Create labels last to keep them on top.

## Shape

Straight line segments. Each line is rasterised once into an anti-aliased image over its bounding box; changing geometry or style re-rasterises it. Good for a few long strokes (paths on a map, dividers), not for many short ones.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Shape.line(x1, y1, x2, y2[, style])` | shape | raise on non-integer or out-of-range coordinate, or bad `style`; nil, reason (table below) | Screen coordinates, `x` in −480..960, `y` in −320..640. |
| `s:set_points(x1, y1, x2, y2)` | nothing | raise as `Shape.line`; nil, reason | Moves the endpoints; the same points again cost nothing. |
| `s:set_style(style)` | nothing | raise on a non-table or bad field; nil, reason | Replaces the **whole** style: omitted fields return to their defaults. |
| `s:set_opacity(a)` | nothing | raise on non-integer (unlike `spr:set_opacity`); no-op | 0..255, clamped. |
| `s:set_z(i)` | nothing | raise on non-integer; no-op | Same child index as `spr:set_z`. |
| `s:set_visible(b)` | nothing | raise; no-op | Show or hide. |
| `s:destroy()` | nothing | — | Frees the slot and its raster budget. |

`reason` values for `Shape.line`, `:set_points` and `:set_style`:

| Reason | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `pool_full` | 8 lines already exist (`line_slots`) |
| `bbox_too_large` | Bounding box plus padding (4 px + half the width on each side) exceeds 480 × 320 |
| `no_mem` | All lines together would exceed the 256 KiB raster budget (`bbox_w * bbox_h * 3` bytes per line), or PSRAM is exhausted |
| `shape_create_failed` | Screen not available |

`style` table, every field optional:

| Field | Type | Default | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `width` | integer | `2` | Clamped to 1..64 |
| `color` | integer | `0xFFFFFF` | `0xRRGGBB` |
| `dash` | `{on, off}` | solid | Exactly two integers, each 0..480; a `0` draws solid. Anything else raises. |
| `cap` | string | `"butt"` | `"butt"` or `"round"`; anything else raises. |

## Anim

Plays a GIF or MJPEG file (`.gif`, `.mjpeg`, `.mjpg`, case-insensitive). Several Anims can be loaded; only one plays at a time. Each loaded Anim holds its whole file plus a `w*h*2` canvas in PSRAM until destroyed. The canvas is opaque RGB565 with no alpha and starts black (`render/lvgl_renderer.c` `renderer_sprite_create_blank`): transparent GIF pixels show black, not what is behind the Anim.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Anim.new(path)` | anim | raise on unknown extension or unsafe path; nil, msg | Loads the file (at most 4 MiB) and creates the canvas; frame size at most 480 × 320. |
| `a:play([loop])` | boolean | raise if `a` is not an anim; `false` on a decode error | `a:play()` plays once; `a:play(true)` or `a:play{loop = true}` loops. |
| `a:pause()` | nothing | raise; no-op | Freezes on the current frame. |
| `a:resume()` | nothing | raise; no-op | Continues after `:pause`; stops any other playing Anim. |
| `a:stop()` | nothing | raise; no-op | Stops and rewinds; the last frame stays on screen until hidden. |
| `a:is_playing()` | boolean | raise; `false` | `false` once a one-shot reaches its last frame: poll it to detect the end. |
| `a:set_pos(x, y)` | nothing | raise on non-integer; no-op | Top-left corner. |
| `a:set_visible(b)` | nothing | raise; no-op | Show or hide. |
| `a:destroy()` | nothing | — | Frees the file buffer and canvas. |

## Speaker

Sounds are aliases declared in `manifest.json` (`audio.sounds`). There is **one channel**: a new `Speaker.play` preempts the current sound, which then receives `on_sound_end(alias, Speaker.REASON_PREEMPTED)`. There is no text-to-speech; every spoken line is a recorded file.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Speaker.play(alias)` | boolean | `false`; `false`: unknown alias, remote alias without a URL yet, within 150 ms of the previous play (`cooldown_reject`), or audio request refused | The automatic restart of a looping sound counts as a play for the cooldown. |
| `Speaker.stop(alias)` | boolean | `false`; `false` if `alias` is not the sound currently playing | `on_sound_end(alias, Speaker.REASON_STOPPED)` arrives at the start of the **next** frame, also when called from inside `on_sound_end`. |
| `Speaker.stop_all()` | `true` | — | Silences everything. |
| `Speaker.is_playing(alias)` | boolean | `false` | `true` while `alias` is the current game sound, by engine bookkeeping (a prediction, not a hardware signal). |
| `Speaker.is_busy()` | boolean | — | `true` while the speaker plays anything, including non-game audio. |
| `Speaker.set_url(alias, url)` | boolean | `false`; `false` for a `path` alias, an undeclared alias or a bad URL | Sets or overrides the URL of an alias declared with `"remote": true` or `"url"`. |
| `Speaker.set_volume(pct)` | nothing | no-op on non-number | 0..100, rounded and clamped. |
| `Speaker.get_volume()` | integer | — | The volume set by the game this session, else the user's saved volume. |
| `Speaker.stats()` | table | — | `{played_total, finish_dropped, error_count, cooldown_reject, no_hookup, speaker_abandoned_current, speaker_abandoned_peak}`. |

Constants: `Speaker.REASON_COMPLETED`, `Speaker.REASON_STOPPED`, `Speaker.REASON_PREEMPTED`, `Speaker.REASON_ERROR`. Compare with the constants, never with numbers.

## Servo

Moves the robot's joints. Aliases come from `servos` and `poses` in `manifest.json`. Commands are queued and sent after `on_tick`; two moves of the same servo in one frame are merged. Results are local predictions, not hardware acknowledgements.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Servo.pose(alias)` | boolean | `false`; `false` for an unknown alias or a full queue | Plays the gesture mapped to a pose alias and marks all four servos busy for about 1.5 s. |
| `Servo.move(alias, angle, duration_ms[, easing])` | boolean | `false`; `false` | Moves one servo. |
| `Servo.stop([alias])` | boolean | `false`; `false` | Stops one servo, or all four without an argument (works even without a `servos` block; `true` only if every stop was queued). |
| `Servo.is_busy(alias)` | boolean | `false` | Predicted from the requested duration, not a hardware signal: fine for "do not queue while moving", not for exact choreography. |
| `Servo.list()` | table | — | `{servos = {alias = "head"\|"base"\|"left"\|"right"}, poses = {alias = gesture}}`. |
| `Servo.stats()` | table | — | `{pushed_total, coalesced_total, dropped_total, sent_total, send_fail_total, back_reject_throttle, back_reject_validation, back_reject_priority, back_reject_queue_full, last_reject_ms, drain_max_us}`; `back_reject_*` count commands the robot refused, by cause. |

## Led

The robot's RGB light. Commands are queued and sent after `on_tick`; the light returns to its previous state when the game ends. Every call returns `false` on bad arguments and never raises.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Led.set(r, g, b)` | boolean | `false`; `false` | Each channel 0..255, rounded and clamped. |
| `Led.off()` | boolean | `false` |  |
| `Led.preset(name)` | boolean | `false`; `false` for an unknown name | One of `user_talk`, `conv_processing`, `robot_talking`, `warm_white`, `light_blue`, `dark_blue`. |
| `Led.blink(r, g, b, period_ms)` | boolean | `false`; `false` when `period_ms` is outside 333..5000 | Rejected, not clamped: at most 3 flashes per second (photosensitivity limit). |
| `Led.pulse(r, g, b, duration_ms)` | boolean | `false`; `false` when `duration_ms` is outside 100..5000 | Lights for `duration_ms`, then turns off. |
| `Led.set_brightness(pct)` | boolean | `false`; `false` when `pct` is outside 0..100 (not clamped) |  |
| `Led.get_brightness()` | integer | — | Last brightness queued successfully (100 until set); not read back from the hardware. |
| `Led.is_available()` | boolean | — | `true` while the game is running; `false` during the top level and `game_start`. |
| `Led.stats()` | table | — | `{pushed_total, coalesced_total, dropped_total, sent_total, send_fail_total, brightness_pct}`. |

## Voice

English keyword spotting: the game sends a short list of command words, the robot listens and reports which one it heard. Not free speech recognition. The pack must list `"voice"` in `peripherals`; otherwise no voice session exists. When it is listed, voice is a hard requirement: if the robot cannot keep the voice connection, it ends the game.

**Start voice from `on_tick`, never from the top level or `game_start`.** The robot sets up the voice session only after `game_start` has returned and drops every voice command queued before that, so keywords sent from `game_start` are lost and nothing is ever heard. Send them in the first `on_tick` (or later, on a scene change).

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Voice.set_keywords(list[, sensitivity])` | `true` | raise if `list` is not a table or `sensitivity` is not a number; nil, reason: `keywords_not_array` (empty table, holes or non-integer keys), `too_many_keywords` (over 64), `too_deep`, `too_many_keys`, `encode_failed` (a function, userdata or thread inside), `payload_too_big` (the whole encoded body over 2047 bytes), `send_failed` | Sends the vocabulary **and starts listening**; opening a session (not in talk-flow) stops the sound that is playing, to keep the speaker out of the microphone. |
| `Voice.start()` | `true` | nil, `"send_failed"` | Not needed: `set_keywords` already starts listening. |
| `Voice.stop()` | `true` | — | Stops listening and closes the session. |
| `Voice.is_available()` | boolean | — | `true` while the game is running (`false` during the top level and `game_start`). |

Each voice frame arrives as `on_voice_event(e)`, decoded from JSON into a table (arrays 1-based, `null` becomes absent). A frame that is not valid JSON or exceeds 8 levels or 256 nodes arrives as the raw string, so check `type(e)`.

| Frame | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `e.type == "VOICE_COMMAND"`, `e.data.keyword` | A keyword from the list was heard. *Shape set by the voice server, not yet confirmed against it ([Q-VOICE-SHAPE](open-questions.md#q-voice-shape)).* |
| `e.type == "VOICE_COMMAND"`, `e.data.status == "unavailable"` | Keyword spotting is down on the server: hide voice hints, keep playing on buttons. |
| `e.type == "error"`, `e.code`, `e.message` | Generated by the robot. `e.code` is one of the codes below. |

| `e.code` | Cause | Game |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `busy` | `set_keywords` while a session is active, or the microphone is in use | continues; the old list stays |
| `no_keywords` | `Voice.start()` with no list sent | continues |
| `no_session_key` | the robot's session key is renewing | continues; retry later with `set_keywords` |
| `invalid_payload` | keyword body too large for the robot | continues |
| `send_failed` | the keyword list could not be sent | continues |
| `connect_failed`, `connect_timeout`, `ws_disconnected`, `ws_error` | the voice connection failed | **ends** |

```lua
local voice_sent = false

function on_tick(dt_ms)
  if not voice_sent then            -- never in game_start: it would be dropped
    voice_sent = true
    Voice.set_keywords({ "jump", "fire", "stop" })
  end
end

function on_voice_event(e)
  if type(e) ~= "table" then return end
  if e.type == "VOICE_COMMAND" and type(e.data) == "table" then
    if e.data.keyword then handle_command(e.data.keyword)
    elseif e.data.status == "unavailable" then hide_voice_hints() end
  elseif e.type == "error" and e.code ~= "busy" then
    hide_voice_hints()
  end
end
```

## Ranking

Leaderboard of the robot game platform. Lua cannot write files; this is the only way to keep a score beyond the session.

| Call | Returns | On failure | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Ranking.report{score = n}` | boolean | `false` when the argument is not a table or `score` is not a number; `false` when sending failed | Submits a score; the engine adds the session duration itself. |
| `Ranking.get_result()` | table or nil | — | The leaderboard fetched after the last successful report, or `nil` if none arrived yet. |

## Sandbox

- Available: the Lua 5.5 base library without `load`, `loadfile` and `dofile`; `string`, `table`, `math`, `utf8`. Not available: `io`, `os`, `debug`, `package`, `coroutine`. Only text chunks load; precompiled bytecode is refused.
- `require("libs/<name>")` loads `libs/<name>.lua` from the pack once per session (later calls return the cached value). Any other module name raises.
- The Lua heap is 512 KiB, garbage included; an allocation past it raises a memory error (in `on_tick` the game ends with `err=OOM`). Image, animation, font and line pixels live in PSRAM outside this heap.
- Nested C calls are limited to 30 levels (desktop Lua: 200). `pcall`, metamethods, `table.sort`/`string.gsub` callbacks and `require` each add a level; deeper nesting raises `C stack overflow`. The parser uses the same counter: a single expression with more than about 20 chained `..` or deeply nested table constructors fails to load on the robot.

## Does NOT exist (commonly invented)

| Invented | Use instead |
| --- | --- |
| `Engine.now_ms(), os.time(), os.clock()` <!-- not-an-api --> | `Timer.millis()` |
| `Engine.version()` <!-- not-an-api --> | nothing; do not print a version from Lua |
| `love.*, update(), draw(), on_draw()` <!-- not-an-api --> | `on_tick` plus retained `Sprite`/`Text` |
| `State.save(), State.load(), any save API` <!-- not-an-api --> | none: nothing persists between sessions; keep scores with `Ranking.report` |
| `Voice.mode()` <!-- not-an-api --> | `params.is_a2a` in `game_start(params)` |
| `Voice.listen(), Voice.transcribe(), speech-to-text` <!-- not-an-api --> | `Voice.set_keywords` plus `on_voice_event` |
| `Speaker.say(), text-to-speech` <!-- not-an-api --> | none: every spoken line is a recorded file |
| `Speaker.play_file("a.wav"), Speaker.play("assets/a.wav")` <!-- not-an-api --> | `Speaker.play("<alias>")` with the alias in the manifest |
| `Sprite.rotate(), spr:rotate(a), spr:scale(k)` <!-- not-an-api --> | `spr:set_rotation(deg10)`, `spr:set_scale(n)` (both sides at most 96 px) |
| `spr:set_alpha(a), spr:set_tint(c), blend modes, filters, gradients` <!-- not-an-api --> | `spr:set_opacity(0..255)`; bake tint, blend and gradients into the image |
| `Sprite.text(), drawing text into a sprite` <!-- not-an-api --> | `Text.new`, or bake the text into the image |
| `Shape.rect(), Shape.circle(), Shape.fill()` <!-- not-an-api --> | `Sprite.solid` for rectangles; circles as images |
| `t:set_width(), t:wrap(), t:set_z(), text measuring` <!-- not-an-api --> | break lines in the data; stack with other objects' `:set_z` |
| `Input.on(), callback registration` <!-- not-an-api --> | the global `on_input(action, phase, hold_ms)` |
| `Timer.after(), Timer.every(), setTimeout` <!-- not-an-api --> | compare `Timer.millis()` with a deadline in `on_tick` |
| `coroutine.*` <!-- not-an-api --> | not loaded; use a state variable and `on_tick` |
| `require("json"), require("socket"), any non-libs/ module` <!-- not-an-api --> | only `require("libs/<name>")` from the pack |
| `io.*, os.*, load, dofile, package.*, debug.*` <!-- not-an-api --> | not loaded (sandbox) |

If a game needs something missing, tell the user and propose an alternative; never invent a call.
